candidates.name: Recursive Hilbert-ball coloring of dyadic partitions driven by a fixed-point-free Lipschitz map
candidates.statement: Fix f: B->B Lipschitz with ||f(x)-x|| >= delta on the unit ball of an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space, and D separated internal dyadic intervals I_1<...<I_D. For a basic partition T, p(T) = f((1/D) sum_j p(T_{I_j})) if T respects every I_j, else 0 (well-founded on cell count). Pull back to F by X_I(g) = p((gT^(n))_I).

final.justification: Survives Tests 1-3. It is not a templated induction strengthening, so the N2 cap does not apply. It is syntactically tiny and occurs nowhere in the goal or L. With it, a 47-year-old problem with at least six failed claims (Shavgulidze 2009, Akhmedov 2009/2013, Beklaryan 2011, Moore 2012, Wajnryb–Witowicz 2014) reduces to about two pages of Hilbert-space algebra. The recursion is forced once the strategy is fixed: the same f must act at every scale so that parent and child pair-correlations share one value alpha. That makes the item low pivot distance GIVEN the strategy, which is the main risk. Downgrade to N2 if (a) the directed arm of P-C1 hits above threshold even with the strategy hidden, (b) an expert names a prior self-similar/recursive nonlinear-map argument for nonamenability, or (c) the proof is found wrong. F1 (extension definition; F3 flavour: a gadget built only to drive the proof).

family_D.rests_on: C1 alone (recursive Hilbert-ball coloring), with C2 as its payoff. All other candidates are N0-N2.
family_D.falls_to: D2 if (a) P-C1's strategy-hidden arms exceed the calibrated threshold; (b) an expert identifies a prior argument that refutes amenability, or bounds Følner sets, via a self-consistent recursive Hilbert- or Banach-valued function and a map without approximate fixed points (none found in the searches listed); or (c) Moore-school folklore turns out to contain the reduction 'F amenable => approximate fixed points for self-similar recursions'. Void (no label) if the proof is wrong.
family_D.not_transfer: The BS map is transfer (N0). The candidate is the recursion that couples the map to F's self-similarity, and no precedent for that coupling was found, so the cross-field-transfer exclusion does not apply.
family_D.correctness_caveat: Conditional on correctness. The family analyst checked every step by hand and found no gap, and the Lean has no sorry/axiom, imports Mathlib only, and its comparator matches the headline exactly. I re-checked the core chain (covariance, translation inequality, recursive identity, energy bounds, alpha cancellation, Jensen/Lipschitz) and agree. But Lean was not built (nanoda off), there is no independent expert confirmation as of 2026-10-09, and the problem has at least six failed claims in both directions.
family_D.compression_note: The proof uses p only through ONE unfolding (X_{I_i}=f(z_i)) plus covariance, so naive inlining is cheap: there is no PHP-style blow-up in the proof term. The Cook–Reckhow analogy is in the search cost (47 years of failed approaches), not in proof-term compression. A 'confirmed eureka' verdict would rest on PLAN step 9 (downstream speedup): e.g. does adding the C1 template help prove nonamenability of other groups (F-like PL groups, Lodha–Moore, Monod's H(A)) or Følner lower bounds?

provenance_flag.explanation: Main theorem: no. Its machinery cites only human work (Følner 1955, BS 1983, CFP 1996, Moore 2013), and no model-produced or AI-assisted precedent for any core item was found. The only 2025-2026 human citations (Guba 2025, 2026) have arXiv versions from 2022-2023, carry no AI disclosure, and are background. Corollaries: yes. Both rest on same-release model-produced OpenAI preprints (families 251 and 214). Grepping the whole release shows no other preprint using Benyamini–Sternfeld or a recursive coloring, so there is no same-vendor architectural precedent (contrast 287/Shlyakhtenko). For Test 4, exclude the 248 preprint, its Lean and docs, and all post-2026-10-06 coverage.

bridge_novelty.import: Nonlinear functional analysis -> amenability: a Lipschitz self-map of the Hilbert ball without approximate fixed points (Benyamini–Sternfeld 1983) used to refute amenability
bridge_novelty.evidence: No prior use of BS/Kakutani/Lin–Sternfeld maps in amenability or group theory found (searches listed in C1.test1). The classical fixed-point/amenability link (Day, Lau, Wiśnicki, Gheysens–Monod, Schneider–Thom) concerns affine or nonexpansive ACTIONS, where amenability implies fixed points. Here the map is not an action, has Lipschitz constant > 1, and a recursion transmits approximate invariance to it. The ingredient is N0; the bridge is the content of C1.
